column1: # POOT-1537 re-sweep, sm_120 rows: the ptxas -v verdict (13.0.88) of every kernel the planner emits for the sweep's shapes, on a secure RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition pod (driver 595.91.07, cuDriverGetVersion 13020; pod 1plioh5jnepuui, 2026-11-12).

# Method (POOT-1509, repeated): every candidate tiling of the eight shapes under the device register model and the lifted one is planned with its tiling pinned and emitted as PTX (llc, sm_80 text); `ptxas -arch=sm_120 -v` reads registers and spill stores; the driver JIT (cuModuleLoadData) gives the same spill verdict for 456 of the 457 distinct PTX. The one exception, `D3 512 narrow 32 ... rows: 2, cols: 1 ... depth: 64` (254 registers), is clean under ptxas and holds 16 bytes of local memory under the driver: its row records the driver's verdict (spills 1), the compiler that runs the kernel.

# Why repeated: the table was swept at POOT-1509 (784 tilings); the attention walk, the gemv and packed contraction run readers, the stable rank and the bf16 dense narrowed contraction (kept bf16, POOT-1535) changed the kernels the planner emits, so 39 of those rows named kernels the planner no longer emits and 81 emitted tilings had no row.
